introduction.p: Each of the following prompts describes a relationship between two quantities. For each, your task is to decide whether or not the relationship can be thought of as a function. If not, explain why. If so, state the domain and codomain of the function and write at least one sentence to explain the process that leads from the collection of inputs to the collection of outputs.

statement.p: The relationship between x and y in each of the graphs below (address each graph separately as a potential situation where y is a function of x). In the lefthand figure, any point on the circle relates x and y. For instance, the y-value \sqrt{7} is related to the x-value -3. In the righthand figure, any point on the blue curve relates x and y. For instance, when x = -1, the corresponding y-value is y = 3. An unfilled circle indicates that there is not a point on the graph at that specific location.

description.p: A plot of the circle of radius 4 centered at the origin.

A plot of a piecewise-defined function g. For x \le 1, g is the quadratic function that passes through (-2,0), (0,4), and (1,3), except g(0) = 1 (that is, there is a hole in the graph at (0,4)). For x \gt 1, g is the linear function with slope -1 that passes through (2,1), except g(2) is undefined (that is, there is a hole in the graph at (2,1)).

answer.p: The circle is not a function of x, but the curve in the right-hand figure is a function of x.

solution.p: The circle is not a function of x, because some values of x correspond to more than one value of y. For example, when x = 0, both y = 4 and y = -4 lie on the circle.
The curve in the right-hand figure is a function of x, because each value of x in the domain corresponds to exactly one value of y.

statement.p: The relationship between the day of the year and the value of the S&P500 stock index (at the close of trading on a given day), where we attempt to consider the index's value (at the close of trading) as a function of the day of the year.

answer.p: The relationship between the day of the year and the S&P500 stock index is a function.

solution.p: The closing value of the S&P500 can be expressed as a function of the day of the year, provided the domain is restricted to trading days (excluding weekends and market holidays). With this restriction, each day in the domain corresponds to exactly one closing value.

statement.p: The relationship between a car's velocity and its odometer, where we attempt to view the car's odometer reading as a function of its velocity.

answer.p: The odometer reading cannot be viewed as a function of the car's velocity.

solution.p: The odometer reading cannot be viewed as a function of the car's velocity. The same speed can occur at many different odometer readings throughout a trip, so a single velocity value can correspond to multiple odometer values.
